bug_description.normalized: When Poppler renders the witness PDF, the Type0 font's attacker-controlled /Encoding stream is parsed as a custom CMap. In CMap::parse2, the stack token buffers tok1/tok2/tok3 are declared without initialization and then reused across keyword dispatch. PSTokenizer::getToken writes only the current token bytes plus a trailing NUL into tok1; the rest of the 256-byte stack buffer stays indeterminate. The witness stream begins with a one-byte token (0xFF) and still provides a following token, so the outer loop runs and then dispatches on tok1 with strcmp(tok1, "/WMode"). That fixed-string comparison reads a 7-byte region from tok1, reaching uninitialized tail bytes beyond the written 0xFF\0 prefix. MemorySanitizer reports the first poisoned byte at offset 2 of that 7-byte read and attributes the poisoned value to tok1's stack allocation in CMap::parse2.

source.description: First project-code statement that consumes the attacker-controlled custom /Encoding CMap stream and materializes vulnerability-relevant data into the stack token buffer tok1.
source.value_from: The witness PDF's Type0 font dictionary uses /Encoding 27 0 R. Object 27 is a malformed stream; the staged PoC bytes show the stream body begins with a single 0xFF byte, which becomes the first token stored in tok1.

tainted_value_origin.description: tok1 is a stack buffer allocated without initialization. Only bytes explicitly written by PSTokenizer::getToken become defined; the untouched tail remains poisoned and is later read by strcmp.

sink.description: MSAN crash site. strcmp dispatch on the partially initialized stack token reads a 7-byte region while matching against the 6-character literal "/WMode" plus NUL, consuming uninitialized bytes from tok1's tail.
sink.note: The sanitizer trace reports uninitialized bytes in __interceptor_memcmp at offset 2 inside a 7-byte region and attributes the poisoned value to the stack allocation of tok1 in CMap::parse2.

root_cause.description: The keyword-dispatch buffer tok1 is stack-allocated without zero-initialization even though later logic compares it to fixed literals with strcmp after PSTokenizer::getToken writes only the token prefix and a terminator.
root_cause.note: CMap::parse2 assumes tok1 is safe for fixed-keyword strcmp after tokenization, but it never initializes bytes beyond the current token length. When the witness CMap produces a one-byte first token, strcmp(tok1, "/WMode") reads into tok1's uninitialized tail. A correct fix would zero-initialize the token buffers before use or avoid fixed-size keyword comparisons on partially initialized storage.

parser_admitted.condition: The witness PDF's /Encoding entry resolves to object 27, which is a stream object, so CMap::parse takes the stream-parsing branch and calls CMap::parse2 on attacker-controlled bytes.

coarse_trace.summary: The fuzzer harness loads the witness PDF and renders its page, driving Poppler's CID font parsing path.
The Type0 font loader reads the /Encoding entry, sees a custom stream-backed CMap, and hands that stream to CMap::parse.

parse2 tokenizes the malformed /Encoding stream into uninitialized stack buffers and dispatches on tok1 with strcmp; the /WMode comparison reads tok1's uninitialized tail and MSAN reports use-of-uninitialized-value.

fine_trace.note: Allocates the stack token buffers without initialization. MSAN later identifies the allocation of tok1 in parse2's stack frame as the origin of the uninitialized bytes observed at the sink.

Reads the first attacker-controlled token from the custom /Encoding stream into tok1. In the witness PoC, the first non-whitespace stream byte is 0xFF, so getToken writes only tok1[0]=0xFF and tok1[1]='\0'; tok1[2..255] stay uninitialized.

Tokenizes the next stream token into tok2 and enters the outer dispatch loop. The witness stream contains additional bytes after the first 0xFF token, so this read succeeds and the strcmp chain below becomes reachable.
The first dispatch compare on tok2 is false for the witness token, so control falls through to the next else-if while tok1 still contains the 1-byte 0xFF token from step 2.

MSAN sink. No guard ensures tok1 has seven initialized bytes before the fixed-keyword comparison. strcmp on "/WMode\0" reads a 7-byte window from tok1; because step 2 initialized only the 0xFF\0 prefix, the compare reaches uninitialized stack bytes in tok1's tail and MSAN reports the first poisoned byte at offset 2.

allocation_context.note: The sanitizer trace says the uninitialized value was created by allocation of tok1 in the stack frame of function CMap::parse2; the actual tok1 declaration is line 235.

cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged fix_commit/patch.diff do not modify poppler/CMap.cc or related custom /Encoding CMap parsing code. The provided patch bundle is therefore unrelated to the witnessed MSAN crash and does not demonstrate the actual fix for this bug.

poc.trigger: The witness is a 334-byte PDF whose page resources define a Type0 font with /Encoding 27 0 R. Object 27 is a malformed stream; its staged bytes show the stream body starts with a single 0xFF token and then additional bytes. When Poppler parses that stream as a custom CMap during page rendering, CMap::parse2 reaches strcmp(tok1, "/WMode") with only the 0xFF\0 prefix of tok1 initialized.

format.name: PDF with custom /Encoding CMap stream
format.contract: A PDF whose Type0 font /Encoding stream begins with a one-byte token (0xFF) and still contains a following token so that CMap::parse2 executes the outer dispatch loop. PSTokenizer::getToken writes only tok1[0]=0xFF and tok1[1]='\0' for the first token; when the next-token dispatch falls through past the false usecmap branch, strcmp(tok1, "/WMode") reads a 7-byte region from tok1 and reaches the uninitialized tail at offset 2. The verified trigger is this exact malformed custom /Encoding stream shape observed in the staged witness PDF, not a generalized class of all invalid CMaps.
